first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation without introducing discount dependence. Verify the strongest onboarding evidence and the competing pricing evidence, focusing on qualified-revenue durability, retention, segment fit, and whether pricing lift persisted after promotions ended. Current memories establish early-funnel gains but do not fully resolve long-term downstream value.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified precedent directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and produced completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning better with sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing despite competitive pressure: its qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention -12% and failure through first renewal. Longer-term retention beyond the observed window remains uncertain, so retain a control and measure qualified activation, retention, and revenue quality.

final2.rationale: Proceed with the onboarding simplification experiment. The acute rise in price-related churn conversations increases urgency but does not overturn verified evidence that a 40% targeted discount raised qualified revenue only temporarily while reducing 30-day retention by 12% and failing through renewal. Shortened onboarding directly addresses the current completion decline and previously improved completion by 13%, time-to-value by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention by 3%. Retain a control and monitor actual churn, qualified activation, retention, and revenue quality; doubled conversations are a warning signal, not yet proof that discounting creates sustainable value.
